site.name: aurora-network
site.summary: Aurora Network — Privacy & Audience (local demo) Fictional social network. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly in a browser. Pages `index.html` — Privacy overview Entry hub. Four cards (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) link to each privacy-management surface. Below the cards, a "Snapshot" panel summarizes the user's current privacy state as a key/value list. `audience.html` — Default audience Radio-group selector with four options (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me). Below the selector: dynamic explanation of who can see new posts, custom-list manager (create / inspect / view recent use), and a "Who can tag you?" radio block. `tag-review.html` — Pending tag queue

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full aurora-network system, prioritizing the primary settings/privacy flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Aurora Network privacy settings flow has functional audience selection and feedback for most actions, but several issues emerge: custom list creation lacks feedback, some links/buttons are non-functional or have small tap targets, and 'Discard changes' fails to provide feedback. Coverage is substantial but only 28% of features were exercised, leaving many untested.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the UX of the aurora-network privacy settings system, covering the primary flow (overview → key subpages) and adjacent states, ensuring mobile responsiveness is validated.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the index (privacy overview), explore each main subpage (audience, tag-review, past-posts, blocked-words) in phases, validate interactables and layout on desktop and mobile. Check for consistency, error states, and recovery paths.
assumptions: All HTML pages load without errors (prescan confirms no load errors)
Interactables (links, inputs, buttons) are functional as per their labels/roles
risk_hotspots: Past post visibility 'apply' action (irreversible bulk change risk)
Tag review 'Approve all'/'Hide all' (batch action risk)

phases.title: Privacy Overview (index.html)
phases.objective: Validate overview page structure, links, and snapshot panel
key_checks: Click each main card link (Default audience, Tag review, Past post visibility, Muted words) and verify navigation
Check 'Snapshot' panel interactables (Change links) for responsiveness
Validate mobile viewport: check small tap targets (links) and layout consistency
exit_criteria: All main links navigate to correct pages
Mobile layout warnings are noted (small tap targets)

phases.title: Default Audience (audience.html)
phases.objective: Test audience selection, custom lists, and tag permissions
key_checks: Select each audience option (Public, Friends, Custom list, Only me) and verify dynamic explanations
Interact with custom list manager (+New list, existing lists) and check state changes
Test 'Who can tag you?' radio block
Validate mobile viewport: check input/button sizes and layout
exit_criteria: All audience options update explanations correctly
Custom list interactions work as expected
Tag permissions radio block is functional
Mobile interactables are usable (despite small tap target warnings)

phases.title: Tag Review (tag-review.html)
phases.objective: Test tag approval/hiding workflows and batch actions
key_checks: Approve/Hide individual tags and verify state changes
Test 'Approve all' and 'Hide all' batch actions
Check 'Block user' action and verify feedback
Validate mobile viewport: check button sizes (batch actions) and layout
exit_criteria: Batch actions (Approve all/Hide all) apply to all pending tags
Mobile batch action buttons are accessible

phases.title: Past Post Visibility (past-posts.html)
phases.objective: Test bulk post visibility changes and filtering
key_checks: Filter posts by year and audience (selectors) and verify visible posts update
Test 'Apply to visible' button (note: simulate action, check feedback)
Check post 'Edit' links for individual post changes
Validate mobile viewport: check filter selectors and 'Apply' button usability
exit_criteria: 'Apply to visible' provides clear feedback (e.g., confirmation/error)
Mobile filters and buttons are usable

phases.title: Muted Words (blocked-words.html)
phases.objective: Test word muting, import/export, and scope settings
key_checks: Add a new word/phrase (type and press Enter) and verify addition
Check 'Where do these apply?' section for clarity
Validate mobile viewport: check input field and button sizes
exit_criteria: Import/Export buttons provide feedback (e.g., file dialog simulation)

coverage_targets.pages: visit all 5 target pages (index, audience, tag-review, past-posts, blocked-words)
coverage_targets.features: exercise all visible controls (links, inputs, buttons, selectors) per page, including batch actions and dynamic content
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks (navigation, batch actions, inputs) on mobile viewport for all pages

notes: Prioritize testing irreversible actions (Past post visibility, Tag review batch) with caution (simulate feedback, not actual bulk changes)
Document small tap target warnings for mobile usability critique

findings.problem: Clicking the '+ New list' button (e.g., in audience.html) provides no visible feedback (e.g., modal, input field) to confirm the custom list creation process was initiated.
findings.evidence: Multiple attempts to click '+ New list' resulted in no UI change (e.g., modal, input field) to indicate the process started. The button is visible but unresponsive or lacks feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Users won’t know if the custom list creation process was initiated, leading to confusion about whether the action succeeded or what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Add immediate feedback (e.g., a modal with an input field, or a confirmation message) when the '+ New list' button is clicked to confirm the process is starting.

findings.user_goal: Interact with custom lists (e.g., 'Close friends', 'Work circle')
findings.problem: Clicking on custom lists (e.g., 'Close friends', 'Work circle') failed due to timeouts, indicating potential issues with interactability or locator accuracy. The lists are visible but may not be interactive.
findings.evidence: Multiple click attempts on custom lists (e.g., 'Close friends') resulted in timeouts, and no UI change occurred. The lists display details (e.g., 28 people, last used 2 days ago) but don’t respond to clicks.
findings.why_it_matters: Users can’t manage or view details of custom lists, limiting their ability to configure audience settings effectively.
findings.suggestion: Ensure custom list elements are interactive (e.g., open a management modal or details page) and verify locators for these elements.

findings.problem: Clicking 'Discard changes' (e.g., in audience.html) provides no visible feedback (e.g., reversion to previous settings, confirmation message) to indicate the action was taken.
findings.evidence: After clicking 'Discard changes', the audience setting remained unchanged (e.g., stayed on 'Only me' or 'Custom list…') with no confirmation message or UI reversion.
findings.why_it_matters: Users won’t know if their changes were discarded, leading to uncertainty about the current audience setting.
findings.suggestion: Add feedback (e.g., a confirmation message or reversion to the previous setting) when 'Discard changes' is clicked to clarify the action’s effect.

findings.problem: Multiple small tap targets (e.g., 'Aurora' link 91x28px, 'Profile' link 358x37px) fall below mobile guidance (44px min), increasing the risk of misclicks.
findings.evidence: Mobile viewport analysis revealed tap targets like 'Aurora' (91x28px) and 'Profile' (358x37px) are smaller than the 44px minimum recommended for mobile touch targets.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets make it difficult for mobile users to interact with elements accurately, leading to frustration and errors.
findings.suggestion: Increase the size of small tap targets (e.g., links, buttons) to at least 44px in height/width for mobile viewports.

findings.problem: Some sidebar links (e.g., 'Profile', 'Account') only add '#' to the URL and don’t navigate to relevant pages, indicating they are non-functional or misconfigured.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Profile' or 'Account' links in the sidebar resulted in the URL updating to include '#' but no navigation to a new page occurred. The links are visible but unresponsive.
findings.why_it_matters: Users can’t navigate to key settings pages (e.g., Profile, Account) via the sidebar, limiting access to important configuration options.
findings.suggestion: Ensure sidebar links (e.g., 'Profile', 'Account') navigate to the correct pages or provide feedback if they are placeholders.

findings.problem: Clicking the 'Import .txt' button (in blocked-words.html) provides no visible feedback (e.g., file dialog, confirmation message) to indicate the import process was initiated.
findings.evidence: Multiple attempts to click 'Import .txt' resulted in no UI change (e.g., file dialog, confirmation message) to confirm the import process started.
findings.why_it_matters: Users won’t know if the import process was initiated, leading to confusion about whether to upload a file or if the action failed.
findings.suggestion: Add feedback (e.g., a file dialog or confirmation message) when 'Import .txt' is clicked to confirm the import process is starting.

findings.user_goal: Export muted words as a .txt file
findings.problem: Clicking the 'Export .txt' button (in blocked-words.html) provides no visible feedback (e.g., file download, confirmation message) to indicate the export process was completed.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Export .txt' resulted in no UI change (e.g., file download, confirmation message) to confirm the export succeeded.
findings.why_it_matters: Users won’t know if the muted words were exported, leading to uncertainty about whether the action succeeded or what to do next.
findings.suggestion: Add feedback (e.g., a file download or confirmation message) when 'Export .txt' is clicked to confirm the export process is complete.

findings.user_goal: Interact with radio buttons on mobile
findings.problem: Radio buttons (e.g., 'Public', 'Friends') in mobile viewports have small tap targets (e.g., 13x62px, 13x42px) below mobile guidance (44px min), increasing misclick risk.
findings.evidence: Mobile viewport analysis revealed radio button tap targets (e.g., 'Public' 13x62px, 'Friends' 13x42px) are smaller than the 44px minimum recommended for mobile touch targets.
findings.why_it_matters: Small radio button targets make it difficult for mobile users to select audience options accurately, leading to errors in privacy configuration.
findings.suggestion: Increase the size of radio button tap targets to at least 44px in height/width for mobile viewports.
